title: Book Publishers Are Quietly Using More AI. Staff Are Revolting
gist: Based on interviews with more than two dozen anonymous workers, WIRED reports that HarperCollins, Simon & Schuster and Hachette are quietly using LLMs for publicity copy, agent emails, cover art and more, often at executive direction and without disclosure to authors. Staff resistance, layoffs-driven workloads, data-privacy concerns and a Skan AI monitoring trial at S&S backed by KKR are fueling an internal revolt.

themes.theme: Quiet AI adoption at the Big Five

insights.claim: At least three of the Big Five US publishers (HarperCollins, Simon & Schuster, Hachette) are quietly using AI tools in publishing without public disclosure or author consent, despite public stances against generative AI.
insights.speaker: Adam Morgan
insights.so_what: A gap between public AI posture and internal practice is a reputational and legal risk for publishers.
insights.quote: quietly incorporating AI tools into their publishing processes without public disclosures or author consent
